title: Combining Functions; Shifting and Scaling Graphs
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar

definitions.title: Algebraic Combinations of Functions
definitions.statement: If f and g are functions with domains D(f) and D(g), their sum, difference, and product are defined on the intersection D(f) \cap D(g). Their quotient f/g is defined on the intersection excluding points where g(x) = 0.
conditions: Domain of f + g, f - g, f * g is D(f) \cap D(g)
Domain of f / g is {x \in D(f) \cap D(g) : g(x) \neq 0}
definitions.explanation: Inputs must be valid for both functions simultaneously. For quotients, zeroes of the denominator function create additional domain exclusions.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Always intersect the domains of individual functions before evaluating combinations.

definitions.title: Composition of Functions
definitions.statement: Given two functions f and g, the composite function f \circ g (also read 'f circle g' or 'f of g') is defined by (f \circ g)(x) = f(g(x)).
conditions: x must be in the domain of the inner function g
g(x) must be in the domain of the outer function f
definitions.explanation: Function composition represents a sequential evaluation: input x first passes through g to produce g(x), which then serves as the input to f. In general, composition is non-commutative: (f \circ g)(x) \neq (g \circ f)(x).
definitions.keyTakeaway: Domain of f(g(x)) requires both x in Domain(g) AND g(x) in Domain(f).

definitions.title: Vertical Shift of a Graph
definitions.statement: Adding a constant k to a function shifts its graph vertically: upward by k units if k > 0, and downward by |k| units if k < 0.
definitions.explanation: The shape, width, and domain of the graph remain identical; the range shifts by k units: [a, b] -> [a+k, b+k].
definitions.keyTakeaway: Adding outside the function shifts vertically.

definitions.title: Horizontal Shift of a Graph
definitions.statement: Subtracting a constant h from the input x shifts the graph horizontally: to the right by h units if h > 0, and to the left by |h| units if h < 0.
conditions: Points (x, y) move to (x + h, y)
definitions.explanation: To achieve the same output value, the new input x must be h units larger than the original input.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Subtracting inside shifts right; adding inside shifts left.

definitions.title: Vertical Stretching and Compressing
definitions.statement: Multiplying f(x) by a positive constant c stretches the graph vertically away from the x-axis by a factor of c if c > 1, and compresses it toward the x-axis by a factor of c if 0 < c < 1.
conditions: x-intercepts remain invariant (f(x) = 0 implies c * f(x) = 0)
Every y-coordinate is scaled by c
definitions.explanation: Vertical scaling affects only the output values without altering the horizontal spacing or the domain.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Multiplying by c > 1 stretches vertically; 0 < c < 1 compresses vertically.

definitions.title: Horizontal Stretching and Compressing
definitions.statement: Multiplying the input x by a positive constant c compresses the graph horizontally toward the y-axis by a factor of 1/c if c > 1, and stretches it away from the y-axis by a factor of 1/c if 0 < c < 1.
conditions: Every x-coordinate is divided by c
definitions.explanation: Multiplying input x by c causes the function to experience its variations c times faster along the x-axis.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Multiplying by c > 1 compresses horizontally by 1/c; 0 < c < 1 stretches horizontally.

definitions.title: Reflections Across Coordinate Axes
definitions.statement: The graph of y = -f(x) is the reflection of y = f(x) across the x-axis. The graph of y = f(-x) is the reflection of y = f(x) across the y-axis.
definitions.explanation: Simultaneously applying both reflections y = -f(-x) produces a point reflection through the origin.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Negative outside reflects over x-axis; negative inside reflects over y-axis.

definitions.title: Standard Equation of an Ellipse via Scaling
definitions.statement: An ellipse centered at the origin with semi-major axis a along x and semi-minor axis b along y is obtained by scaling the unit circle x^2 + y^2 = 1 horizontally by factor a and vertically by factor b.
conditions: When a = b = r, the ellipse reduces to the circle of radius r
definitions.explanation: Substituting x/a for x and y/b for y in the circle equation demonstrates that stretching a circle by unequal factors along the coordinate axes generates an ellipse.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Ellipses are circles whose coordinate axes have undergone independent horizontal and vertical scalings.
